title: Dave Rowntree - Wikipedia
notes: David Alexander De Horne Rowntree, born 8 May 1964, Colchester, Essex; his mother a viola player, his father a BBC sound engineer. Percussion at the Landermere Music School at weekends; percussion with his father in the Colchester Silver Band, a brass band. An HND in Computer Science at Thames Polytechnic, then a programmer for Colchester Borough Council. Played in bands with Graham Coxon growing up; Coxon's father taught jazz classes at Landermere. Joined Blur in 1989 when Coxon introduced him to Damon Albarn. Every Blur studio album from Leisure (1991) to The Ballad of Darren (2023); drums on two tracks of Gorillaz (2001); later a solicitor, a Labour councillor and candidate, an animator and a composer for television; a solo album, Radio Songs (2023).

title: Dave Rowntree: "If I can't write about myself on my solo record, when can I?" (V13, February 2023; read in the Wayback Machine's copy)
notes: 'Ginger Baker, for all his faults and I can't imagine he's a particularly nice man but he was a drumming hero of mine growing up, he wrote some music books for aspiring drummers which I worked through religiously.' Baker's philosophy in the introduction to one: the audience have paid money, so tell them something.

title: Hitmakers: The songwriting secrets behind Blur's Parklife (Ben Homewood, Music Week, 29 July 2024)
notes: Rowntree on Parklife: 'Quite dramatically, on Parklife, I started adding in offbeats and slanting the rhythms'; 'I came off the beats and I added in the funk. That's where my rhythmic sense lies.' He quotes Bootsy Collins: 'Even that band Blur, they have the funk, deep down'. Recorded at Maison Rouge and RAK.

title: Dave Rowntree - drummerszone.com profile
notes: Taught 'the hard way' by 'a gargantuan Scotsman'; Saturday jazz classes run by Graham Coxon's father; plays timpani too; Fat Les. Gives 'Dorset, 1968' for his birth, against Wikipedia's Colchester, 1964.

title: How I Got That Sound: Stephen Street (Sound On Sound)
notes: Song 2: 'two drum kits set up in the room with Dave Rowntree and Graham Coxon hitting out a rhythm', recorded on the room mics (a Neumann U87) to sound 'lo-fi and small'; Street chose a few bars and 'copied, pasted and repeated it until I had my drum loop that ran the duration of the song'; he had made drum loops with Blur before.

title: Leisure (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 August 1991 (Food); Madchester and shoegaze influences; Stephen Street produced There's No Other Way among seven tracks. Dave Rowntree drums, percussion.

title: Parklife - Wikipedia
notes: Released 25 April 1994 (Food), produced by Stephen Street; recorded at Maison Rouge from August 1993. Singles Girls & Boys, To the End, Parklife, End of a Century. Dave Rowntree drums, percussion, programming, crowd noise.

title: The Great Escape (Blur album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 11 September 1995 (Food); singles Country House (Blur's first number one, against Oasis's Roll With It), The Universal, Stereotypes, Charmless Man. Produced by Stephen Street.

title: Blur (Blur album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 February 1997 (Food), produced by Stephen Street, recorded from June 1996 at Mayfair and in Reykjavik; the band jammed for the first time, Street cutting loops from the jams. Rowntree: 'We just played together for two weeks in a way we hadn't done since 1991'; 'a much more aggressive record'. Graham Coxon additional drums on Song 2 and Strange News from Another Star; On Your Own uses a Roland TR-606.

title: 13 (Blur album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 15 March 1999, produced by William Orbit, recorded June-October 1998 in London and Reykjavik. Rowntree: 'Things were starting to fall apart between the four of us.' Dave Rowntree drums, percussion; Jason Cox additional drums on Battle. Rolling Stone heard 'shambling drum loops'.

title: Girls & Boys (Blur song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 7 March 1994. Alex James: 'Disco drums, nasty guitars and Duran Duran bass.' Rowntree 'admitted that he is not playing on the track, being replaced by a drum machine he programmed', and called it his favourite song on the 2000 Best Of because he 'isn't really in it'.

title: Song 2 - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 7 April 1997; two minutes and two seconds; Coxon suggested playing Albarn's slow demo fast and loud. Personnel: Graham Coxon guitar, additional drums; Dave Rowntree drums.
